# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Extend storyline options with conditional and cost-gated effects

## Problem statement

The generalised storyline option model (`StorylineOption`) currently supports
only a label, a single successor, and an apply/skip effect policy. Content and
engine authors cannot express options that are only available when the player
can afford them, that branch to different successors based on game state, or
that carry their own extra effects. The game-agnostic seam
(`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) was explicitly designed to grow into these
semantics, and this capability was deliberately deferred from the
`write-storylines` epic as speculative until now.

## Users

- **Engine/content authors** — need richer per-option semantics (affordability
  gates, state-based branching, extra effects) without bypassing the
  game-agnostic seam or hand-writing bespoke engine code per card.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need the extension to stay declarative,
  serialisable, statically validatable, and portable to the core engine.
- **Players** — should only be offered choices they can actually take, and
  should have their decisions reflected accurately in coins/reputation.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — must keep selecting legal, presented options so
  headless games never stall or pick a hidden/unaffordable branch.

### Example user stories

- "As an engine author, I want to gate an option behind a coin/reputation cost,
  so the choice only appears when the player can afford it."
- "As a content designer, I want an option's successor to depend on coins or
  reputation, so one choice can lead down different branches."
- "As a content designer, I want an option to apply an extra effect on top of
  its apply/skip policy, so choices can have their own consequences."
- "As a developer, I want invalid cost/condition data to fail the validator, so
  mis-authored storylines cannot ship."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Backwards-compatible model extension.** `StorylineOption` gains optional
   `cost`, `extraEffect` (`{ coins?: number; reputation?: number }`), and
   ordered `conditionalSuccessors` (`{ when: { field: 'coins'|'reputation';
   op: '>='|'<='|'>'|'<'|'=='; value: number }; successorId }`) fields. Omitting
   all three preserves today's behaviour exactly — verified by the existing
   legacy-equivalence and C1 regression harness passing unchanged.
   *Metric: unit tests + existing regression harness pass with zero behavioural deltas.*

- **Cost gating.** An option whose `cost` exceeds the player's current
   coins/reputation is **omitted** from the presented option list; available
   options are computed and stored with the pending choice so resolution
   indexing, transcript tokens, and save/load stay stable. Selecting an
   affordable option deducts the declared cost as an additional payment,
   independent of its `effectPolicy`, and applies any `extraEffect`.
   *Metric: unit tests assert exact coin/reputation deltas, omission, and stable indexing.*

- **Conditional successors.** `conditionalSuccessors` is evaluated in order;
   the first matching rule wins, and the option's `successorId` is the fallback
   when none match. Above/below threshold, equality boundary, and no-match
   fallback cases are covered, including succeeding-card push.
   *Metric: unit tests for each boundary/fallback case.*

- **Static validation & schema.** The validator and manifest schema reject
   invalid new data — negative/empty cost, malformed conditions (unknown field
   or op, non-numeric value), and dangling conditional successors — while the
   shipped CSVs validate cleanly and the doc-drift test passes.
   *Metric: validator unit tests with broken fixtures + clean run on shipped content.*

- **AI / Monte Carlo integration.** `decideEventChoice` (and the generalised
   AI selection path) chooses only among presented/affordable options and
   accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas; the regression and Monte Carlo
   harnesses run to completion without stalls.
   *Metric: AI policy tests + regression/Monte Carlo harness green.*

- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (option model, resolution
   lifecycle, roadmap), the migration notes in `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`,
   and the CSV column reference in `src/README.md` (confirming the new
   semantics remain programmatic, not CSV-authored).
   *Metric: doc-drift test passes; reviewer confirms docs match code.*

- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
   *Metric: full test suite green.*

## Constraints

- **Programmatic authoring only (producer decision Q1=A).** Extend the
  in-memory model, engine resolution, validator, and schema. Keep the legacy
  CSV at the two-way Accept/Reject shape; do **not** add CSV columns for the
  new semantics.
- **Declarative and serialisable (producer decision Q3=A).** Only
  field/op/value conditions and numeric deltas. Arbitrary callbacks are out of
  scope here — see the follow-up work item below.
- **Game-agnostic seam.** New semantics must live behind
  `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` and keep the future core-engine extraction
  viable (pure/declarative data, no Main-Street globals baked in beyond the
  injected template registry).
- **Affordability is coins and/or reputation (producer decision Q2.1).** A cost
  may specify either or both; an option is available only when *all* specified
  costs are affordable.
- **Omit, do not disable (producer decision Q2.2).** Unaffordable options are
  removed from the presented list, not shown greyed out.
- **Cost is a real payment (producer decision Q2.3).** Deducted from the
  player in addition to the option's apply/skip effect policy.
- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  gameplay must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.

## Existing state

- `StorylineOption` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts`) = `{ label, successorId,
  effectPolicy }`. `CompiledStoryline` wraps an ordered option list.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` compiles legacy `hasChoices` /
  `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId` into `[Accept, Reject]`, and supports
  explicit multi-way lists via `registerStorylineOptions(eventId, options)`.
  `getStorylineOptions(event)` is pure (no state) and is used by callers,
  the validator, and the graph exporter.
- `resolveStorylineOption(state, event, option)`
  (`src/MainStreetStoryline.ts`) applies `effectPolicy` and pushes
  `option.successorId`; `resolveEventOption(state, optionIndex)`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) indexes the option list, records the
  transcript, and drives `pushChainCard`.
- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) returns a binary
  `'accept' | 'reject'` and reasons about `coinDelta` / `reputationDelta`,
  `projectEventCoinDelta`, `eventSeverity`, and successor severity.
- Validation lives in `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts`; the manifest/schema
  in `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` and
  `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`; docs in
  `docs/main-street/storylines.md` (§2 model, §3 lifecycle, §9 seam, §10
  roadmap).
- `PendingEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`) currently stores
  `{ event, chosenOption, resolved }`.

## Desired change

Extend the option model and resolution path so that:

1. Options declare an optional affordability `cost`; the presented option list
   is filtered to affordable options before the dialog/AI sees it, and the
   filtered list is stored with the pending choice.
2. Options declare an optional `extraEffect` and ordered
   `conditionalSuccessors`, both applied/selected at resolution time using the
   declarative predicate vocabulary.
3. Selection deducts `cost`, applies `extraEffect` independently of
   `effectPolicy`, and pushes the first matching conditional successor (or the
   default `successorId`).
4. The validator, schema, and graph/manifest export understand the new fields;
   the AI policy operates over the presented option list.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — Extend `StorylineOption` with `cost`,
  `extraEffect`, and `conditionalSuccessors`; add a `Condition` type.
- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — Filter options by affordability, apply cost +
  extra effects, resolve conditional successors; expose a state-aware
  accessibility accessor alongside the pure `getStorylineOptions`.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Store the presented/available option list on
  `PendingEventChoice` so indexing and save/load remain stable.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` uses the stored
  presented list; update logging/transcript for cost and extra effects.
- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice` selects only among
  presented options and accounts for cost/extra-effect deltas.
- `src/scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — Validate cost/condition/effect data and
  conditional successor targets.
- `src/scripts/storyline-graph.ts` + `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json`
  — Represent and validate the new option metadata in the manifest/graph.
- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — Document the extended option model and
  resolution semantics; update the seam/migration notes.
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storyline-graph.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/storylines-doc-drift.test.ts` — New/extended coverage.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV` — **write storylines** (completed epic; parent context).
- `MS-0MUMP93DI0018OGV` — **Storyline model & extraction seam** (completed; the
  generalised `StorylineOption` this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP92O9002772U` — **Storyline behaviour regression harness** (completed;
  the byte-for-byte regression guard).
- `MS-0MUMP944B009PEO6` — **Static validator & npm gate** (completed; the
  validator this extends).
- `MS-0MUMP95IW002ARWJ` — **Storyline authoring helper CLI** (completed).
- `MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0` — **Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema**
  (completed; manifest/schema this extends).
- `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N` — **Support arbitrary callback conditions/successors in
  storyline options** (follow-up, medium priority, `discovered-from` this item).
- Roadmap entry: `docs/main-street/storylines.md` §10.

## Risks

- **Option-index drift.** Filtering options changes the index space; the
  pending-choice list must be frozen at draw time or the UI, AI, and transcript
  can disagree. *Mitigation:* store the presented list on
  `PendingEventChoice` and resolve by index into it.
- **AI divergence.** `decideEventChoice` is currently binary; a generalised
  selector that ignores affordability/cost could pick a hidden option or stall.
  *Mitigation:* route AI through the same presented list; cover with
  regression/Monte Carlo tests.
- **Manifest/schema churn.** Adding optional fields can break the graph export
  or doc-drift test. *Mitigation:* keep new fields optional and update schema,
  exporter, and docs in the same change.
- **Scope creep.** Arbitrary callbacks, CSV authoring, and per-option animation
  are explicitly out of scope; the callback escape hatch is tracked separately
  as `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Delivery surface.** How far should this change reach?
  - Answer (producer): **A** — extend the in-memory model + engine resolution +
    validator/schema only, programmatically via `registerStorylineOptions`;
    keep the legacy CSV at two-way Accept/Reject. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Cost-gated semantics.**
  1. What gates eligibility?
     - Answer (producer): **coins and/or reputation**. Source: interactive reply.
  2. When unaffordable, omitted or shown disabled?
     - Answer (producer): **omitted**. Source: interactive reply.
  3. Is the cost deducted on selection in addition to apply/skip?
     - Answer (producer): **yes**. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Conditional successors & per-option extra effects representation.**
  - Answer (producer): **A** — declarative, serialisable data
    (`extraEffect` + ordered `{ when, successorId }` rules with `successorId`
    fallback). Additionally: create a **medium-priority follow-up work item**
    to add arbitrary callbacks. Source: interactive reply. Follow-up created as
    `MS-0MUPORT1Z000QX8N`.

### Assumptions

- No shipped card content is expected to use the new semantics; existing
  legacy/card behaviour must remain byte-for-byte equivalent.
- Because a pending choice blocks all player actions, the set of affordable
  options is stable between draw and resolution; storing the presented list on
  the pending choice makes this explicit and save/load-safe.
- Cost deduction that drops coins or reputation to zero triggers the normal
  loss checks (no special-casing).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUO8B93V002CL06** – Help panel content drifts from PRD milestone 5 (7 sections, >8 lines) (in-progress)
- **MS-0MUOSII720060IZQ** – Implement free market re-roll mechanic (engine + state + bias draw) (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMP94S7008KTI0** – Storyline graph/manifest export & JSON schema (completed)

- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, accessibility, actions, actually (+276 more)

# Intake brief: Re-sync generated Vite config's watcher-ignore so main-checkout dev servers and test runs stop exhausting inotify (ENOSPC)

## Problem statement

Running the full test suite from the main checkout fails with repeated
`ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` (17 vite-node CLI
test failures in the latest run) because the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively
traverses `.worklog/worktrees/**` — 18 worktree checkouts totalling ~7 500 extra
files — exhausting the machine-wide `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` (65 536) under
concurrent processes. The repo's checked-in `vite.config.ts` predates (and never
received) the core scaffold template's watcher-ignore guard that fixes exactly
this failure mode, so the bug persists on every main-checkout dev server start
and test run.

## Users

- **Developers/agents maintaining main-street** — must be able to run the test
  suite and dev server from the main checkout without host-wide watcher limits
  being hit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer, I want `npm test` and `npm run dev` to work
    from the main checkout so I can verify changes and the audit skill's F3
    re-runs without tripping a host inotify limit."
- **Audit/verification tooling** — the post-push belt-and-suspenders validation
  and the audit skill's cache-miss auto-execution depend on a green main-checkout
  suite.
  - *User story:* "As the verification pipeline, I want the full suite to pass
    from the main checkout so finished work can be independently confirmed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `vite.config.ts` wires the shared ignore list into the Vite file watcher:
   it imports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin`
   and sets `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]`, and that list
   contains `**/.worklog/**` — verified by a unit regression test that mirrors the
   core `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC guard and asserts the real config file.
2. Starting the Vite dev server (and the Vitest projects) from the main checkout
   registers **no** watchers under `.worklog/**` — asserted deterministically via
   `server.watcher.getWatched()` keys (or equivalent), ported from the core
   `vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts` AC3/AC4 pattern.
3. A full test-suite run from the **main checkout** (via the test skill) completes
   with no ENOSPC watcher failures — the 17 previously failing vite-node CLI tests
   pass.
4. No regression to existing behaviour: the `unit` / `unit-cli` project split
   (MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG), dev-output watch handling (`data`, `tmp`, `results`,
   `dist`), and `resolvePagesBase`/`cardResultsWriterPlugin` remain intact.
5. Related documentation updated to reflect the ENOSPC guard and the
   `.worklog/**` watch exclusion (config comment matching the template wording;
   README/dev-notes as applicable). CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship
   skill's release pipeline.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- `vite.config.ts` is declared AUTO-GENERATED by `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`,
  and the current template (core submodule pinned at `dc4ec0ce`) **already** emits
  the watcher guard — do **not** modify the core template or any `core/` file.
- **Do not blind re-scaffold** (`npm run scaffold`): the current template lacks this
  repo's local `unit-cli` project isolation (MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG), `CLI_TEST_FILES`,
  `cardResultsWriterPlugin`, and `resolvePagesBase` additions; a blind re-scaffold
  would regress them. Apply a surgical sync of the `server.watch.ignored` block only.
- Host-level tuning (raising `fs.inotify.max_user_watches`) is **out of scope** —
  it is privileged and masks the root cause; the fix must require no kernel changes.
- Stale-worktree pruning (4+ worktrees for completed items — MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4,
  MS-0MUYFXBC4003073C, MS-0MV2DPSVB004B1WX, `f7-competitive-before-85d23dbb`) is an
  operational prerequisite for a clean main-checkout validation run, gated on
  operator approval for others' worktrees (cleanup skill) — not part of this code
  change.
- Test-execution policy: all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill.

## Existing state

- `vite.config.ts` `server:` block has `port`/`open` only — no `watch.ignored` —
  so the watcher walks `.worklog/worktrees/**` (18 worktrees, ~7 457 files / 624
  dirs outside `node_modules`, measured) and exhausts inotify under concurrent
  runs. Measured machine-wide watch usage 18 535 / 65 536 at idle — headroom is
  intermittent, not guaranteed.
- The core scaffold template already contains the guard and core regression tests
  assert it (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed, CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV); `tce-the-rising`
  has the generated block, main-street never received the re-sync.
- Failure evidence: post-push main-checkout suite reruns fail only with ENOSPC
  referencing stale worktree paths; the worktree finish-gate full suite passes green.

## Desired change

- Import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin`
  and add `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` to the existing
  `server:` block, with a short comment explaining the `.worklog/worktrees` ENOSPC
  guard (matching the template/tce-the-rising wording). All local project fixtures
  (`unit`, `unit-cli`, `browser`) stay untouched.
- Add a unit regression test asserting the real config wires the ignore list and
  that `.worklog/**` is covered (e.g. `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`,
  alongside the existing `tests/deploy/vite-*` config tests).

## Key Files:

- `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored`; document the guard
- `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — regression: config wires ignore list; `.worklog/**` covered; no `.worklog` paths in `server.watcher.getWatched()` (pattern with `tests/deploy/preview-smoke.test.ts` / core's `vite-transcript-plugin-regression.test.ts`)
- `README.md` / dev docs — note the `.worklog/**` watch exclusion and main-checkout run guidance, as applicable

## Related work

- MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C — [test-failure] `<suite exited 1>`: `npm --silent test` (completed; same root suite-exit failure mode)
- MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4 — Colour card faces by synergy type (completed; the item whose finish exposed the ENOSPC recurrence)
- MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG — [test-failure] Main Street vite-node CLI tests flake under vitest file-level parallelism (completed; the `unit-cli` project isolation that a blind re-scaffold would regress)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template-side fix — this item ports it into main-street's checked-in config)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening and deviation items (completed)
- **Discovered:** the same missing `server.watch.ignored` block exists in 8 sibling game repos (AI_Hell, tce-beleaguered-castle, tce-blackjack, tce-coloretto, tce-feudalism, tce-golf, tce-lost-cities, tce-sushi-go) — tracked as a separate derived work item, out of scope here.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption:** the durable, testable deliverable is the checked-in config sync;
  worktree pruning and host tuning are operational/privileged and outside the repo
  change (recorded in the brief, not the ACs). (OPEN QUESTION if the operator wants
  them in scope after all.)
- **Risk (low):** chokidar ignore-glob semantics — `**/.worklog/**` matches the
  `.worklog/worktrees/**` tree; validated by the core regression suite and the
  deterministic watcher assertion in AC2. Mitigation: port the same assertion
  pattern used in core tests.
- **Risk (medium):** config-test flakiness from real dev-server startup under
  parallelism — mitigation: keep the watcher-population assertion best-effort/deterministic
  like the core regression test (AC2), and rely on AC3's full-suite run for the
  end-to-end guarantee.
- **Risk (scope creep):** sibling-repo porting, worktree pruning, and host tuning
  are tempting adds — recorded as related work items/notes, not this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No interactive clarifying questions were required: the item's description
  (with the operator-approved remediation list) plus repo evidence fully resolved
  the problem, root cause, and intended fix.
- Research summary: root cause isolated to the missing `server.watch.ignored`
  guard in the checked-in `vite.config.ts` (the core scaffold template at submodule
  `dc4ec0ce` already emits it; core tests CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA guard it; the
  generated file predates the change). Evidence: `vite.config.ts` (no watch block),
  `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (template has it), `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`
  (assertion), `.worklog/worktrees/` (18 stale checkouts), inotify usage measurement.
- Decision: issue type corrected `chore` → `bug` (current behaviour is broken —
  dev server and test runs crash with ENOSPC); priority stays `medium`
  (infra/verification friction, not a blocked pipeline). Host tuning and pruning
  recorded as out-of-scope/related (see above).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV** – Core scaffold template Pages base (completed)
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** – Port Vite watcher-ignore (server.watch.ignored) to sibling game repos' generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MUSY1K6B00095AT** – Storyline editor test harness & fixtures (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: able, ac4, acceptance, add, adds (+295 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: able, acceptance, add, adds, agent (+232 more)
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: 0mv5sehhg000zkua, able, ac2, add, adds (+185 more)

Generalise the `storylines:graph` conventions into a dev-only diagram generator

# Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version

## Problem statement

`npm run build` silently compiles against whatever commit happens to be checked out in the `./core` submodule (currently `dc4ec0ce`, v0.1.21-3-gdc4ec0ce), and nothing ever updates it. Dev builds can therefore skew from the latest engine without anyone noticing, while release builds are not reproducible because nothing records which engine commit they were built against.

## Users

- **Game developer (internal)** — wants dev builds to always compose the latest Tableau Card Engine so behaviour is tested against current engine code. User story: "As a game developer, I want `npm run build` to pull the engine's latest remote HEAD, so my builds reflect current engine behaviour without manual submodule surgery."
- **Release operator (maintainer)** — wants deterministic, reproducible release builds. User story: "As a release operator, I want release builds to compile against exactly the engine SHA recorded in a committed pin file, so a release can be reproduced bit-for-bit from source."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run build` (and `npm run build:electron`) runs an `engine:sync` step before compiling: `git submodule update --remote core` fetches the latest remote HEAD of whatever branch `core` tracks and checks it out. The build fails loudly (never clobbers) if `./core` has uncommitted changes.
2. `npm run build:release` runs an `engine:verify` step instead: it reads the committed pin file `configs/engine-pin.json` (engine SHA), checks out exactly that SHA, and fails the build if the pinned SHA differs from the remote-resolved target or contains local modifications.
3. `configs/engine-pin.json` holds a single `sha` field (e.g. `{"sha": "dc4ec0c..."}`) and is written only by the release process (alongside the version bump) — never by dev builds.
4. The `engine:sync` / `engine:verify` npm scripts are independently invocable (`npm run engine:sync`, `npm run engine:verify`) and covered by unit tests for the dirty-state guard and pin-mismatch failure paths.
5. The build-script template change is made in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (engine repo) and main-street is re-scaffolded so a future re-scaffold does not clobber the change. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related documentation (docs/dev, README/DEPLOYMENT as applicable) is updated.

## Constraints

- **No CI beyond npm builds** — there is no separate CI pipeline; `npm run build` is the verification vehicle. Release pinning is enforced at tag/merge time only, not by a CI job.
- **Scaffold ownership** — `package.json` scripts and `vite.config.ts` in main-street are scaffolded from `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (engine repo). The dev/release script change must land in that template, then main-street is re-scaffolded; editing only the generated copy gets clobbered.
- **`git submodule update --remote` must never overwrite dirty submodule state** — fail loudly instead.
- Core's remote default branch is `main`; the submodule may be checked out detached or tracking a branch — sync must behave correctly for either.

## Existing state

- `.gitmodules` declares `core` → `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine.git`.
- `package.json` has `build: "tsc --noEmit && vite build"` and `build:electron`; no `build:release`, no engine sync/verify steps.
- Submodule currently at `dc4ec0ce` (v0.1.21-3-gdc4ec0ce), never auto-updated.

## Desired change

- Add `engine:sync` (dev auto-update + dirty guard), `engine:verify` (pin check + exact checkout), and `build:release` scripts; wire `engine:sync` into `build`/`build:electron` and `engine:verify` into `build:release`.
- Introduce `configs/engine-pin.json` owned solely by the release process.
- Update the scaffold template in the engine repo (`core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) so generated game repos get the same scripts; re-scaffold main-street.

## Key Files

- `package.json` — new `engine:sync`, `engine:verify`, `build:release` scripts; `build` / `build:electron` wiring.
- `scripts-*` (generated via `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) — new engine sync/verify script that the npm scripts invoke; located in the engine repo template and re-scaffolded into main-street.
- `configs/engine-pin.json` — new committed pin file (`{"sha": "..."}`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — engine-repo template to update so re-scaffolds carry the new behaviour.
- `vite.config.ts` — generated; verify re-scaffold preserves any needed changes (no manual edits expected).
- `docs/dev/*` — build/release documentation to reflect dev/release split.

## Related work

- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV — "Core scaffold template Pages base" (completed): precedent for the cross-repo process of editing the core scaffold template and re-scaffolding this repo; the implementation consideration in this item mirrors it.
- MS-0MV5928XV0007X1J — "Cross-repo: core pack-asset byte seam + submodule bump" (completed): precedent for bumping the `core` submodule pointer as part of main-street work.
- MS-0MV76P7BN00164RF — "Toneforge should be off by default" (completed): documents the cross-repo submodule-bump discipline.
- MS-0MUQ1KXAS003FJ42 — "Ship web-based copy of Main Street (GitHub Pages)" (completed): release/deployment pipeline context.
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — "Load the committed ToneForge runtime synth module" (completed): submodule-bump precedent.
- MS-0MV16VZWP001OUNR — "Full-suite verification & release readiness" (completed): release-gating precedent.
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` / `core/AGENTS.md` — engine-repo docs to update when the scaffold template changes.
- MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED risk note: a bad `engine:sync` could land a broken engine commit in dev builds; mitigation is the loud-failure dirty guard and the pin/verify split.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: auto-sync lands a broken engine commit.** Dev builds silently move to a newer engine that may be red on its own suite. Mitigation: `engine:sync` is loud about what it changed and dirty-state guard prevents clobbering; the pinned release path is the safety net.
- **Risk: dirty `./core` submodule.** `git submodule update --remote` refuses when uncommitted changes exist; we must surface that as an explicit build failure, not a silent skip.
- **Risk: network/remote dependence.** Dev builds now require reachable GitHub at build time; offline builds fall back to current checkout with a warning (assumption — confirm behaviour during implementation).
- **Risk: scope creep** — pin-file metadata (tags, dates), CI jobs, or Steam/Electron packaging integration are out of scope; record as linked work items if needed.
- **Assumption:** core's tracking branch may change; sync follows whatever branch `core` tracks (operator answer Q2-A), which matches the submodule's configured remote branch.
